name: Customs, export and trade compliance
one_line: The cross-border trade-compliance situation on the logistics schema: declarations, tariff classification and valuation, origin and preference evidence, export licences, broker correspondence, customs holds and release notices tied to one consignment or movement. Its distinctive relation is not simply goods moving; it is a declarant or representative supplying a customs authority with a classification, origin, procedure and value that determines permission, duty or release. Shipment custody, warehouse movements, procurement and manufacturing records can appear in the same packet but are separate readings. This placeholder serializes no destination fields because the logistics schema is deferred under PR-6.

node_test.why: LEG 1 — SIGNALS. The logistics default recognizes custody and movement: parties, goods, quantity, places, carrier and acknowledgement. Customs/export narrows that relation to a cross-border declaration or control case: a movement or consignment reference is joined to declarant/importer/exporter roles, commodity classification, origin, customs procedure, valuation, licence or preference evidence, duty treatment and a release/hold status. A bill of lading, invoice, shipment number or border crossing alone is not customs evidence. LEG 2 — DIMENSIONS, conditional because PR-6 forbids serialization. The logistics default is carrier or counterparty -> consignment/container -> record_type, with vehicle/depot/day alternatives. Customs is consignment or movement-led -> record_type, optionally carrier or declarant above it only where that improves retrieval; jurisdiction is a value, not a field or dimension. Customs procedure, commodity code, origin and status are values inside records, not default folders. LEG 3 — PRIVACY. Customs files expose declared values, product composition, tariff strategy, origin suppliers, importer/exporter identifiers, tax registrations, licences and trade-sensitive routes. That concentrated commercial and regulatory exposure warrants potentially_sensitive treatment and local/redacted handling, without inventing a P7 class.
node_test.charge_answered: The strongest objection is that a customs declaration is already one work type under logistics, or a duplicate of a shipment record. The row survives because customs documents are authority-facing control instruments: the declaration's declarant, procedure, tariff classification, origin, valuation and release state determine whether goods may cross and how they are treated. A consignment note or packing list can support shipment custody while the same bytes independently support customs. If a corpus contains only transport documents, purchase invoices or generic border vocabulary without a declaration/control structure, this template should be refused and those files should remain with shipment, procurement or a residual.

deterministic: a customs declaration structure with a movement/entry reference, labelled declarant or representative, importer/exporter roles, commodity or tariff classification, customs procedure, country of origin, customs value or valuation method, duty/tax treatment and release/hold status

an export-control or licence structure that joins exporter, goods classification, destination/end user, licence or authorization reference, quantity/value and conditions; a generic business licence or certificate does not qualify
a certificate-of-origin or preference structure with exporter, producer or origin declaration, goods/commodity lines, origin criterion, consignee or movement reference and issuing/attesting role
a tariff-classification or customs-ruling file with goods description, candidate or assigned commodity code, classification rationale, ruling authority/reference and effective scope

a customs-broker entry or duty-account statement joining one consignment or movement reference to declarant/importer roles, classification, customs value, duty/tax amounts, clearance status and broker fees
a customs hold, inspection, seizure or release structure with declaration/movement reference, authority action, reason/code, examination or document request, status and release/next-step evidence

a bonded-warehouse or transit procedure record joining goods and container references to customs procedure, seal, warehouse/transit location, guarantee/security, inspection and discharge/arrival status
a manifest or EDI customs payload whose labelled segments contain declarant/importer/exporter roles, commodity lines, origin, procedure, value and customs status; format alone never activates

an archive manifest containing a declaration, commercial invoice, packing list, origin evidence, licence and broker/release correspondence for one movement; archive contents are inspected without extraction
a customs portal screenshot or OCR scan whose own headings, movement reference, authority status and declaration fields establish a customs case rather than a generic shipment image

template.why: Empty by placeholder contract: logistics declares no legal fields. Subject to R1c licensing the anchor's proposals, the customs recommendation is consignment or movement -> record_type, with carrier or site only when they are explicit and materially improve retrieval. Declarant/importer/exporter roles, jurisdiction, commodity code, origin, procedure, duty and release status are record values or search evidence, not folder dimensions. This differs from the logistics default's carrier/counterparty -> consignment -> record_type because customs is authority-control-led and the same movement may involve several brokers or authorities; a carrier name must not collect unrelated customs cases. It is not time-first; the design says, "For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders." The user may reverse, remove or flatten any later order.

collides_with.signal: Direction one — logistics.customs-export owns the authority-facing declaration/control evidence when a movement or consignment reference joins declarant/importer/exporter roles to classification, origin, procedure, valuation and release or hold. Direction two — logistics.shipment owns custody and movement evidence joining carrier, consignor, consignee, goods, packages, places, vessel/vehicle and acknowledgement, even when a customs declaration is attached. SAME FIXTURE BYTES: `Commercial-Invoice-Packing-List-Bill-of-Lading-and-Customs-Entry.pdf`. Customs declaration and authority-status pages support this row; bill-of-lading, package and carrier custody pages support shipment. A port, container, commodity or movement number alone supports neither.

Direction one — logistics.customs-export owns the customs procedure, authority hold/release and declaration evidence governing whether goods may move across the border. Direction two — logistics.warehouse-ops owns physical receipt, bin, quarantine, pick, dispatch and inventory movements while goods are in depot custody, whether or not a customs hold is noted. SAME FIXTURE BYTES: `Bonded-Warehouse-Entry-and-Customs-Release.xlsx`. Customs procedure and release-status sheets support this row; pallet, bin, quantity and warehouse event rows support warehouse operations. A bonded location, hold word or quantity alone supports neither.

Direction one — logistics.customs-export owns declaration content, commodity classification, origin, value, duty and clearance status for a movement. Direction two — business_operations.corporate-regulatory-filings owns the enterprise filing obligation, deadline, declaration/signature control, submission reference, acknowledgement and compliance trail, whether the filing concerns customs or another regulator. SAME FIXTURE BYTES: `Annual-Customs-Declaration-and-Compliance-Submission.xlsx`. Goods-line and customs calculation sheets support this row; filing calendar, approval, acknowledgement and exception-control sheets support business operations. A reporting period, authority name or submission reference alone supports neither.

Direction one — logistics.customs-export owns the authority-facing import/export control instrument and its movement-specific classification, origin, valuation and release. Direction two — business_operations.procurement-sourcing owns supplier selection, tender, purchase award, landed-cost comparison and buying approval, even when duty or origin is an input. SAME FIXTURE BYTES: `Import-Purchase-Order-and-Customs-Dossier.pdf`. Declaration and release pages support customs; supplier quote comparison, purchase approval and sourcing pages support procurement. A supplier, price, country or commodity code alone supports neither.

Direction one — logistics.customs-export owns the declaration, origin, tariff, duty and clearance evidence for goods crossing the border. Direction two — retail_hospitality.supplier-order owns a hospitality buyer's order, supplier confirmation, ordered quantities, delivery window and receipt, whether the goods are imported. SAME FIXTURE BYTES: `Restaurant-Import-Customs-and-Supplier-Order.pdf`. Customs entry and authority-status pages support this row; menu/stock-related order lines, supplier confirmation and delivery terms support supplier-order. Food, supplier, country or delivery vocabulary alone supports neither.

Direction one — logistics.customs-export owns the movement's declaration, tariff/origin, value, export-control and release evidence. Direction two — manufacturing.production-record owns product/lot genealogy, material consumption, process execution, inspection and production release, even when a lot is exported. SAME FIXTURE BYTES: `Export-Lot-Customs-Packet.pdf`. Customs declaration and exit confirmation support this row; batch record, lot genealogy and manufacturing release pages support production. A lot, product code, package or export word alone supports neither.

Direction one — logistics.customs-export owns the movement-specific declaration, origin and export-control evidence for an imported or exported consignment. Direction two — manufacturing.supplier-qualification owns the supplier's capability, approval scope, quality audit and ongoing qualification status, even when origin or customs records are reviewed. SAME FIXTURE BYTES: `Supplier-Origin-Certificate-and-Qualification-Review.pdf`. Origin/certificate and customs movement pages support this row; supplier capability, audit and approval pages support supplier-qualification. A supplier name, certificate or country alone supports neither.

Direction one — logistics.customs-export owns customs declaration, licence, duty and release facts for the movement. Direction two — business_operations.contract-administration owns the ongoing administration of a freight, broker, trade or supply agreement: clauses, notices, fees, variations, indemnities, disputes and obligation tracking. SAME FIXTURE BYTES: `Broker-Agreement-and-Customs-Entry-Dispute-Pack.pdf`. Customs entry/status pages support this row; contract clauses, service-level notices and fee dispute pages support contract administration. A signed agreement or broker fee alone supports neither.

falls_through_to.why: An isolated broker confirmation, duty payment receipt, delivery confirmation or clearance email without a recoverable declaration/control group is transactional evidence.
falls_through_to.design_cite: Receipts and Confirmations may hold isolated invoices, delivery confirmations, booking records, boarding passes, purchase receipts, event tickets, and similar transactional documents.

falls_through_to.why: A standalone certificate, licence, ruling, customs notice or durable form with no accepted movement or control case remains an independent record.
falls_through_to.design_cite: Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.

falls_through_to.why: An ambiguous invoice, declaration draft, portal screenshot, OCR scan, calendar event or mixed packet whose customs role cannot be settled needs review rather than inferred movement facts.
falls_through_to.design_cite: Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision.

falls_through_to.why: An unreadable customs portal export, protected archive or damaged declaration cannot establish authority, movement or release from its filename.
falls_through_to.design_cite: Unsupported or Encrypted may hold—or, more safely, represent without moving—password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats.

falls_through_to.why: Declared values, importer identifiers, licences, tariff strategy, product composition and trade-sensitive routes may require protected local treatment when no safe accepted group exists.
falls_through_to.design_cite: Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts.

sensitivity_why: Customs records can expose importer/exporter and tax identifiers, declared values, product composition, tariff strategy, origin suppliers, export licences, controlled-goods destinations, broker accounts and trade routes. This row assigns no handling class and does not make those raw values destination dimensions.
open_question: NEEDS-JOSEPH NJ-CUSTOMS-1: should `consignment` remain the sole safe customs parent, or should R1c license a neutral movement/case field distinct from shipment custody? A private `customs_movement` key is not minted here. NJ-CUSTOMS-2: should declarant/importer/exporter roles remain search-only because they are organization/identity collectors, or may user-approved branches expose one role for retrieval? NJ-CUSTOMS-3: when one packet contains customs declaration, shipment custody, purchase order and manufacturing lot evidence, should all schemas coactivate independently on disjoint sections, or should user policy select one packet owner?
